newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia removes Gulf War scar from capital.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia removes Gulf War scar from capital.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, trying to erase the scars of the 1991 Gulf War, has destroyed a building that was damaged by Iraqi Scud missiles more than six years ago, a Saudi newspaper said on Thursday.
Al-Eqtisadiah business daily said authorities destroyed the office building in the capital Riyadh and removed the rubble in preparation for a new one.
"The building, which until the date it was struck by the Iraqi missile had served as a population registry office, remained as a witness to the Iraqi aggression," it said.
Saudi Arabia hosted U.S.-led troops from more than 30 countries which ousted the Iraqi army from the Gulf state of Kuwait in 1991.
Iraq fired Scud missiles at Saudi Arabia and arch-foe Israel during the war.
Al-Eqtisadiah said that children who had grown up with the image of the building with its destroyed western side would no longer need to ask questions.
"Heavy machines removed the building the day before yesterday in preparation to build it anew and to erase the bad image it left for seven years," the paper said.
